tests.title: A whitespace-only positional argument is folded into the bare-invocation case before Resolve runs, with no model resolution attempted
given: no vendor credential environment variable is set, so a model-resolution attempt would fail loudly and distinguishably
tests.when: App.Main is invoked with the positional argument "   " (three spaces) and a writable --dir
then: the process exit code is ExitUsage (2), not the ExitFailed/auth failure a reached model resolution would produce
fs.Usage() still prints the help text and flag list to stderr, unchanged
tests.pseudocode: code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--dir", dir, "   "}, emptyStdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert code == ExitUsage; assert strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "usage")

tests.title: A bare invocation with stdout not a terminal emits a usage envelope naming the four accepted input shapes
given: stdout is a bytes.Buffer, which isTerminal reports as not a terminal
tests.when: App.Main is invoked with an empty positional argument
then: exactly one JSON object is written to stdout
ok is false, exit_code is 2, status is "usage"
error.stage is "usage" and error.category is "usage"
error.message equals "no input: give a report, a file path, a GitHub or GitLab issue URL, or - to read stdin"
the returned process exit code is 2
tests.pseudocode: code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--dir", dir}, emptyStdin, &stdout, &stderr); env := unmarshal(stdout); assert code == 2 && !env.OK && env.Status == "usage" && env.Error.Message == "no input: give a report, a file path, a GitHub or GitLab issue URL, or - to read stdin"

tests.title: A bare invocation with stdout a terminal writes nothing to stdout
given: stdout is an *os.File opened on a character device (e.g. /dev/null, which isTerminal treats identically to a tty since it only checks os.ModeCharDevice); the test is skipped where no such device is available
tests.when: App.Main is invoked with an empty positional argument
then: stdout receives zero bytes
the process exit code is still 2
the help text is still printed to stderr, unchanged from today
tests.pseudocode: f, _ := os.OpenFile(os.DevNull, os.O_RDWR, 0); code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--dir", dir}, emptyStdin, f, &stderr); assert code == 2; info,_ := f.Stat(); assert info.Size() == 0

tests.title: -h/--help and --version exit before the bare-invocation check and never emit an envelope
given: stdout is a bytes.Buffer (not a terminal), so the bare-invocation envelope would fire if the check were reached
tests.when: App.Main is invoked once with only -h and once with only --version
then: for -h, stdout stays empty and the process exit code is 0
for --version, stdout carries the version sentence and no JSON object, and the process exit code is 0
tests.pseudocode: code1 := app.Main(ctx, []string{"-h"}, stdin, &out1, &err1); assert code1 == ExitOK && out1.Len()==0; code2 := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--version"}, stdin, &out2, &err2); assert code2 == ExitOK && !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(out2.String()), "{")

tests.title: The bare-invocation envelope's error.message is byte-identical to the message toolio.ErrNoInput's own path produces
tests.when: the error.message from a bare invocation (stdout not a terminal) is compared against the error.message produced when Resolve itself returns ErrNoInput (e.g. stdin piped as "-" with only whitespace on it)
then: both messages are the exact same string: "no input: give a report, a file path, a GitHub or GitLab issue URL, or - to read stdin"
tests.pseudocode: envBare := runBareInvocation(); envStdin := runApp([]string{"--dir", dir, "-"}, "   \n"); assert envBare.Error.Message == envStdin.Error.Message

tests.title: status and summary are always present, never omitted, on every envelope regardless of outcome
given: a Run whose result implements no Summary() interface
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called once with ExitOK and once with ExitFailed
then: both marshalled envelopes carry a non-empty "status" key
both marshalled envelopes carry a "summary" key that is present even though no tool supplied one
tests.pseudocode: for _, code := range []int{ExitOK, ExitFailed} { env := run.Envelope(code, plainResult, errInfoOrNil); b,_ := json.Marshal(env); assert bytes.Contains(b, []byte(`"status"`)); assert bytes.Contains(b, []byte(`"summary"`)) }

tests.title: status is derived one-to-one from the exit code, in both directions, for every code in the table
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called once for each of ExitOK, ExitFailed, ExitUsage, ExitNeedsHuman and ExitUnverified
then: status equals done, failed, usage, needs_human and unverified respectively
status never disagrees with ok or exit_code for any of the five
tests.pseudocode: table := map[int]string{ExitOK:"done", ExitFailed:"failed", ExitUsage:"usage", ExitNeedsHuman:"needs_human", ExitUnverified:"unverified"}; for code, want := range table { env := run.Envelope(code, nil, errInfoFor(code)); assert env.Status == want }

tests.title: A Result implementing Summary() supplies the envelope's summary, truncated to 200 characters
given: a stub Result type whose Summary() string method returns a 250-character sentence
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called with ExitOK and that result
then: envelope.summary has length exactly 200
envelope.summary equals the first 200 characters of the stub's returned string
tests.pseudocode: type stub struct{}; func (stub) Summary() string { return strings.Repeat("x", 250) }; env := run.Envelope(ExitOK, stub{}, nil); assert len(env.Summary) == 200

tests.title: A Result with no Summary() falls back to error.message when ok is false
given: a plain struct result with no Summary() method
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called with ExitFailed and an ErrorInfo whose Message is "the pull request could not be opened"
then: envelope.summary equals "the pull request could not be opened"
tests.pseudocode: env := run.Envelope(ExitFailed, plainResult{}, &ErrorInfo{Stage:"land", Category:"forge", Message:"the pull request could not be opened"}); assert env.Summary == "the pull request could not be opened"

tests.title: A Result with no Summary() falls back to "<tool>: done" when ok is true
given: a Run named "fix"
a plain struct result with no Summary() method
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called with ExitOK
then: envelope.summary equals "fix: done"
tests.pseudocode: run := NewRun("fix", "v1"); env := run.Envelope(ExitOK, plainResult{}, nil); assert env.Summary == "fix: done"

tests.title: A high-severity warning on an ok:true run appends a fixed, deterministic clause noting the count and severity to the summary
given: a Run carrying two warnings: one severity "high", one severity "low"
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called twice, with ExitOK and a result whose Summary() returns "fix: committed and landed"
then: envelope.summary starts with "fix: committed and landed"
envelope.summary also states that 1 high-severity warning is present and that the highest severity is high
the appended clause text is identical across both calls, given the same warnings
tests.pseudocode: run.Warn(WarnCode("input_truncated"), "high", "cut"); run.Warn(WarnCode("comment_not_posted"), "low", "not posted"); env1 := run.Envelope(ExitOK, summaryStub{"fix: committed and landed"}, nil); env2 := run.Envelope(ExitOK, summaryStub{"fix: committed and landed"}, nil); assert strings.HasPrefix(env1.Summary, "fix: committed and landed"); assert strings.Contains(env1.Summary, "1") && strings.Contains(env1.Summary, "high"); assert env1.Summary == env2.Summary

tests.title: The envelope's JSON keys are emitted in the fixed field order, with usage.phases last
given: an Envelope carrying every optional field: status, summary, error, needs_human, warnings, result, input, usage, model
tests.when: the Envelope is marshalled with encoding/json
then: the key order in the raw JSON text is tool, version, ok, status, exit_code, summary, error, needs_human, warnings, result, input, usage, model, duration_ms, started_at
within the usage object, "phases" is the last key
tests.pseudocode: b,_ := json.Marshal(fullEnvelope); order := extractTopLevelKeyOrder(b); assert order == []string{"tool","version","ok","status","exit_code","summary","error","needs_human","warnings","result","input","usage","model","duration_ms","started_at"}; usageOrder := extractKeyOrder(b, "usage"); assert usageOrder[len(usageOrder)-1] == "phases"

tests.title: needs_human carries question, options, needed, stage and a non-literal resume template when status is needs_human
given: an ErrorInfo with Stage "analyse"
a result reporting a question and two options A/B, with no needed value
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called with ExitNeedsHuman (3) and a large (50KB) input body
then: needs_human.question is set from the tool's question
needs_human.options carries both A and B entries, and needed is omitted
needs_human.stage equals error.stage exactly ("analyse")
needs_human.resume matches the fixed template naming the invocation shape and contains no fragment of the 50KB input text
tests.pseudocode: env := run.Envelope(ExitNeedsHuman, questionResult, &ErrorInfo{Stage:"analyse", Category:"ambiguous", Message:"..."}); assert env.NeedsHuman.Stage == "analyse"; assert !strings.Contains(env.NeedsHuman.Resume, largeInputBody); assert len(env.NeedsHuman.Options) == 2 && env.NeedsHuman.Needed == ""

tests.title: needs_human is omitted entirely when status is not needs_human
given: a result that could otherwise supply a question
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called with ExitOK, ExitFailed, ExitUsage and ExitUnverified
then: the marshalled JSON contains no "needs_human" key for any of the four
tests.pseudocode: for _, code := range []int{ExitOK, ExitFailed, ExitUsage, ExitUnverified} { env := run.Envelope(code, questionResult, errInfoFor(code)); b,_ := json.Marshal(env); assert !bytes.Contains(b, []byte(`"needs_human"`)) }

tests.title: codefix's Ambiguity maps onto needs_human's question and options A/B
given: a codefix.Result with Ambiguity{Question: "...", InterpretationA: "the HTTP client's retry loop", InterpretationB: "the job queue's redelivery"}
tests.when: the codefix pipeline's own envelope-facing shape is read by toolio.Run.Envelope while assembling the envelope with ExitNeedsHuman
then: needs_human.question equals the Ambiguity's Question
needs_human.options equals [{id:"A", text: InterpretationA}, {id:"B", text: InterpretationB}]
tests.pseudocode: result := &codefix.Result{Ambiguity: &codefix.Ambiguity{Question:"...", InterpretationA:"the HTTP client's retry loop", InterpretationB:"the job queue's redelivery"}}; env := run.Envelope(toolio.ExitNeedsHuman, result, &toolio.ErrorInfo{Stage:"analyse", Category:"ambiguous"}); assert env.NeedsHuman.Options[0] == Option{ID:"A", Text:"the HTTP client's retry loop"}

tests.title: codeimpl's Blocker maps onto needs_human's question and needed, with no options
given: a codeimpl.Result with Blocker{Reason: "the spec names a module the PRD does not create", Needed: "a decision on module X"}, set by the survey phase
tests.when: toolio.Run.Envelope assembles the envelope with ExitNeedsHuman from that Result
then: needs_human.question equals Blocker.Reason
needs_human.needed equals Blocker.Needed
needs_human.options is omitted
tests.pseudocode: result := &codeimpl.Result{Blocker: &codeimpl.Blocker{Reason:"the spec names a module the PRD does not create", Needed:"a decision on module X"}}; env := run.Envelope(toolio.ExitNeedsHuman, result, &toolio.ErrorInfo{Stage:"survey", Category:codeimpl.CategoryBlocked}); assert env.NeedsHuman.Question == result.Blocker.Reason; assert env.NeedsHuman.Needed == result.Blocker.Needed; assert len(env.NeedsHuman.Options) == 0

tests.title: checkUpstream sets Result.Blocker naming the dependency and the upstream package when a dependency is neither sealed nor done
given: a spec package B declaring a task dependency on spec package A
spec package A has status "active" (not sealed) with at least one task not yet done
tests.when: codeimpl.Run is invoked against spec package B
then: the run exits with code 3 (ExitNeedsHuman)
result.Blocker.Reason names the dependency (spec A)
result.Blocker.Needed names the upstream package
the resulting envelope's needs_human is populated the same way any other blocker is (question from Reason, needed from Needed, no options)
tests.pseudocode: writeSpecPackage(t, specADir, "01", "upstream"); markOneTaskUndone(specADir); writeSpecPackage(t, specBDir, "02", "downstream", dependsOn: "01"); result, err := codeimpl.Run(ctx, codeimpl.Options{Input: specBInput, ...}); assert result.Blocker != nil && strings.Contains(result.Blocker.Reason, "01"); assert strings.Contains(result.Blocker.Needed, "upstream")

tests.title: specgen never sets needs_human even when open_questions is non-empty; the summary reports only the count
given: a specgen.Result with three OpenQuestions entries
tests.when: toolio.Run.Envelope assembles the envelope for an ExitOK run on that result
then: needs_human is omitted
result.open_questions still carries all three entries, unaffected
envelope.summary mentions that 3 open questions remain
tests.pseudocode: result := &specgen.Result{Package: specgen.Package{OpenQuestions: threeQuestions}}; env := run.Envelope(toolio.ExitOK, result, nil); b,_ := json.Marshal(env); assert !bytes.Contains(b, []byte(`"needs_human"`)); assert len(result.OpenQuestions) == 3; assert strings.Contains(env.Summary, "3")

tests.title: Repeated --context flags render one labelled block appended to the phase prompt, independently of Body, and are reported as input.context_bytes
given: --context "first note" and --context "second note" are both given on the command line, in that order
tests.when: toolio.Common's flags are parsed and the run proceeds through App.execute
then: the rendered block is headed "## Additional context from the caller" with one paragraph per value, in the order given
Input.Body is unchanged by --context: it equals exactly what Resolve produced
the phase prompt construction appends the block separately from Body
envelope.input.context_bytes equals the rendered block's byte length
tests.pseudocode: common.Context = []string{"first note", "second note"}; block := common.ContextBlock(); assert strings.HasPrefix(block, "## Additional context from the caller"); assert strings.Contains(block, "first note") && strings.Contains(block, "second note"); in := resolveInput(); assert in.Body == originalBody; env := run.Envelope(...); assert env.Input.ContextBytes == len(block)

tests.title: An input plus context block exceeding MaxInputBytes is refused as a usage error before anything is fetched
given: Body is 200000 bytes long
one --context value brings len(Body)+len(contextBlock) above toolio.MaxInputBytes (256KB)
tests.when: the run is invoked with that input and --context value
then: the process exits with code 2
error.category is "usage"
no network call or file read is made for the input
neither Body nor the context block is silently truncated
tests.pseudocode: body := strings.Repeat("a", 200000); ctxVal := strings.Repeat("b", 70000); env, code := runApp([]string{"--dir", dir, "--context", ctxVal, body}); assert code == toolio.ExitUsage; assert env.Error.Category == "usage"; assert !networkCalled

tests.title: retryable is true only for the api and aborted categories, for any category in the shared vocabulary
tests.when: for any category in {usage, input, auth, model, invalid_spec, blocked, ambiguous, empty_change, internal, budget, max_turns, no_result, unverified, git, forge, disk, api, aborted}, an ErrorInfo of that category is built by toolio
then: retryable is true exactly when category is "api" or "aborted", and false for every other category in the domain
tests.pseudocode: for cat := range allCategories { info := toolio.BuildErrorInfo(cat, ...); want := cat == "api" || cat == "aborted"; assert info.Retryable == want }

tests.title: error.resumable is set from the result's Resumable() method via a type assertion
given: a stub Result type with Resumable() bool
tests.when: Run.Envelope is called with a failing exit code and, in turn, a stub returning true and one returning false
then: error.resumable equals the stub's return value in both cases
tests.pseudocode: type stubT struct{ v bool }; func (s stubT) Resumable() bool { return s.v }; env1 := run.Envelope(ExitUnverified, stubT{true}, errInfo); env2 := run.Envelope(ExitUnverified, stubT{false}, errInfo); assert env1.Error.Resumable == true; assert env2.Error.Resumable == false

tests.title: codefix.Result.Resumable always returns false, because branch names are never deterministic
given: a codefix.Result with Branch set to a non-empty value, e.g. "fix/issue-42-abcdef"
tests.when: Resumable() is called on it
then: it returns false regardless of whether Branch is set
tests.pseudocode: r := codefix.Result{Branch: "fix/issue-42-abcdef"}; assert r.Resumable() == false; r2 := codefix.Result{}; assert r2.Resumable() == false

tests.title: codeimpl.Result.Resumable returns true exactly when Branch is non-empty
given: one codeimpl.Result with Branch = "impl/09-widget"
one codeimpl.Result with Branch = ""
tests.when: Resumable() is called on each
then: the first returns true
the second returns false
tests.pseudocode: assert codeimpl.Result{Branch:"impl/09-widget"}.Resumable() == true; assert codeimpl.Result{Branch:""}.Resumable() == false

tests.title: specgen.Result.Resumable returns true exactly when SplitPlan is non-empty

tests.title: issuetriage.Result.Resumable always returns false
given: an issuetriage.Result with every field populated as a filed issue would be
tests.when: Resumable() is called on it
then: it returns false

tests.title: fix_hint for the budget and max_turns categories names the flag, the resolved current bound, and a suggestion double it
given: a run whose resolved per-phase Bounds has MaxBudgetUSD=2.0 and MaxTurns=20
tests.when: an ErrorInfo of category "budget" and one of category "max_turns" are built from those Bounds at a non-"budget" stage
then: the budget error's fix_hint is {flag: "--budget", current: 2.0, suggest: 4.0}
the max_turns error's fix_hint is {flag: "--max-turns", current: 20, suggest: 40}
tests.pseudocode: bounds := agentrun.Bounds{MaxBudgetUSD:2.0, MaxTurns:20}; hintB := toolio.FixHintFor("budget", "implement", bounds, nil); assert hintB == FixHint{Flag:"--budget", Current:2.0, Suggest:4.0}; hintT := toolio.FixHintFor("max_turns", "implement", bounds, nil); assert hintT == FixHint{Flag:"--max-turns", Current:20.0, Suggest:40.0}

tests.title: fix_hint for the no_result category takes the shape of whichever bound the phase actually stopped at
given: an agentrun.NoResultError exposing RunStopBudgetExceeded
a second agentrun.NoResultError exposing RunStopMaxTurns
tests.when: toolio builds the fix_hint for each of the two no_result errors
then: the first's fix_hint has flag "--budget"
the second's fix_hint has flag "--max-turns"
tests.pseudocode: errBudget := agentrun.NoResultError("implement", "submit", agentrun.Result{StopReason: agentrun.RunStopBudgetExceeded}); errTurns := agentrun.NoResultError("implement", "submit", agentrun.Result{StopReason: agentrun.RunStopMaxTurns}); assert toolio.FixHintFor("no_result", "implement", bounds, errBudget).Flag == "--budget"; assert toolio.FixHintFor("no_result", "implement", bounds, errTurns).Flag == "--max-turns"

tests.title: fix_hint for the auth category names the vendor's credential variables, or the forge token names for a forge credential
given: a model auth failure whose vendor's CheckCredentials table lists ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
a forge auth failure targeting GitHub
tests.when: toolio builds the fix_hint for each
then: the model auth fix_hint is {env: ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", ...]}
the forge auth fix_hint for GitHub is {env: ["GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN"]}
tests.pseudocode: modelHint := toolio.FixHintFor("auth", "preflight", bounds, anthropicAuthErr); assert contains(modelHint.Env, "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"); forgeHint := toolio.FixHintFor("auth", "land", bounds, githubForgeAuthErr); assert forgeHint.Env == []string{"GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN"}

tests.title: fix_hint for the model category is the static tier list, regardless of what model spec was asked for
tests.when: an ErrorInfo of category "model" is built for an unresolvable model spec
then: fix_hint equals {flag: "--model", valid: ["SIMPLE", "STANDARD", "ADVANCED"]}
tests.pseudocode: hint := toolio.FixHintFor("model", "preflight", bounds, unresolvableModelErr); assert hint.Flag == "--model" && hint.Valid == []string{"SIMPLE","STANDARD","ADVANCED"}

tests.title: fix_hint for a usage error naming exactly one culprit flag is present; one naming none or several is omitted
given: a usage error from issue combining --overwrite with --repo/--label
a usage error from fix combining --no-verify with --verify
a generic usage error naming no specific flag
tests.when: toolio builds the fix_hint for each
then: the first two carry fix_hint {flag: "--overwrite"} and {flag: "--no-verify"} respectively
the third has no fix_hint field at all
tests.pseudocode: h1 := toolio.FixHintFor("usage", "usage", bounds, errors.New("--overwrite cannot be combined with --repo or --label")); assert h1.Flag == "--overwrite"; h2 := toolio.FixHintFor("usage", "usage", bounds, errors.New("--no-verify cannot be combined with --verify")); assert h2.Flag == "--no-verify"; h3 := toolio.FixHintFor("usage", "usage", bounds, errors.New("expected one input, got 2")); assert h3 == nil

tests.title: A budget-category error whose stage is literally "budget" gets a --total-budget fix_hint instead of the per-phase --budget one
given: a run with TotalBudgetUSD=10.0 and a per-phase MaxBudgetUSD=2.0
an ErrorInfo{Stage: "budget", Category: "budget"} from codeimpl's total-budget check
a second ErrorInfo{Stage: "implement", Category: "budget"} from an ordinary per-phase ceiling
tests.when: toolio builds the fix_hint for each
then: the first's fix_hint is {flag: "--total-budget", current: 10.0, suggest: 20.0}
the second's fix_hint is {flag: "--budget", current: 2.0, suggest: 4.0}
tests.pseudocode: h1 := toolio.FixHintFor("budget", "budget", bounds, totalBudgetErr /* carries TotalBudgetUSD:10.0 */); assert h1.Flag == "--total-budget" && h1.Current == 10.0 && h1.Suggest == 20.0; h2 := toolio.FixHintFor("budget", "implement", bounds, nil); assert h2.Flag == "--budget" && h2.Current == 2.0

tests.title: Run.Warn accepts a WarnCode and severity, and the envelope reports each warning as a code/severity/stage/message object
tests.when: Run.Warn(WarnCode("input_truncated"), "high", "the input was truncated at %d bytes", 262144) is called

tests.title: every declared WarnCode constant has an entry in the stage table

tests.title: a source scan flags a Run.Warn call site that passes a bare string literal instead of a declared WarnCode

a fixture source file containing a call shaped like Warn("some_code", "high", "message")

tests.title: severity is read as given at the call site, not derived from code alone

tests.title: the WarnCode stage table carries every code-to-stage pair the spec lists
tests.when: every listed pair (input_truncated/input, comments_unreadable/input, no_verify_command/preflight, criteria_unmet/implement, commit_not_parked/park, checkout_not_restored/park, pull_request_not_opened/land, comment_not_posted/report, spec_edit_reverted/task, state_not_saved/park, draft_package/preflight, upstream_missing/preflight, parked_attempt_discarded/preflight, spec_validation_warning/preflight, specs_dir_unreadable/preflight, project_language_unknown/preflight, name_flag_ignored/usage, scope_renamed/prd, scope_count_mismatch/prd, split_plan_foreign/split, split_plan_unreadable/split, split_plan_stale/split, split_plan_update_failed/split, split_plan_not_removed/split, architecture_not_written/write, activation_failed/activate, rejected_path_calls/analyse) is looked up in the declared table
then: every pair is present and matches exactly

tests.title: docs/cli.md's output example includes status, summary and needs_human fields
tests.when: docs/cli.md is read
then: the documented output example carries the keys "status", "summary" and "needs_human"
tests.pseudocode: body := readFile("docs/cli.md"); assert strings.Contains(body, "\"status\"") && strings.Contains(body, "\"summary\"") && strings.Contains(body, "\"needs_human\"")

tests.title: docs/cli.md's error-category table gains a retryable column and a new warning-codes table
tests.when: docs/cli.md is read
then: the error-category table has a column header naming "retryable"
a separate warning-codes table is present listing WarnCode entries with a severity and a stage column
tests.pseudocode: body := readFile("docs/cli.md"); assert strings.Contains(body, "retryable"); assert strings.Contains(body, "input_truncated") && strings.Contains(body, "severity") && strings.Contains(body, "stage")

tests.title: docs/cli.md documents --context under the shared flags section
tests.when: docs/cli.md is read
then: the shared flags section names "--context" and describes it as repeatable
tests.pseudocode: body := readFile("docs/cli.md"); assert strings.Contains(body, "--context")

tests.title: README.md's exit-code sentence names the matching status value for each of the five exit codes
tests.when: README.md is read
then: the exit-code sentence names "done", "failed", "usage", "needs_human" and "unverified" alongside 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively
tests.pseudocode: body := readFile("README.md"); for _, s := range []string{"done","failed","usage","needs_human","unverified"} { assert strings.Contains(body, s) }

tests.title: A program-driven caller invoking fix with no argument and stdout redirected to a file gets one parseable envelope
given: stdout is redirected to a real file, not a terminal
no positional argument is given
tests.when: the fix binary's shared App.Main runs end to end through the real toolio shell
then: the process exits with code 2
the file holds exactly one JSON object with status "usage" and error.message naming the four accepted input shapes
the caller can parse that file and read error.message to correct the invocation

tests.title: fix stops on an ambiguity and resumes with --context to reach a done analysis
given: a report describing a bug with two plausible causes
a real git repository workspace
tests.when: fix is run once with the report, stops on the ambiguity, and is run a second time with the same input plus --context "<answer>"
then: the first run's envelope has status "needs_human" with needs_human.options carrying entries A and B and a resume template naming the invocation shape
the second run's rendered context block reaches the analyse phase's prompt
the second run completes with status "done"

tests.title: impl hits a per-phase budget ceiling and resumes on the same branch once the ceiling is raised
given: a real spec package under .specs with at least one task
a per-phase --budget ceiling low enough that a task phase exceeds it
tests.when: impl is run once against the spec, stops at the budget ceiling with Result.Branch already set, and is run a second time with a higher --budget
then: the first run's envelope carries error.category "budget", error.fix_hint {flag: "--budget", current, suggest}, and error.resumable true because Branch is non-empty
the second run continues on the same branch and completes with status "done"

tests.title: A high-severity input-truncation warning surfaces in an otherwise successful fix run's summary
given: a report exceeding toolio.MaxInputBytes is given as fix's input
a real git repository workspace
tests.when: fix runs end to end and lands the change
then: the envelope's warnings array carries one entry with code "input_truncated", severity "high", stage "input"
envelope.ok is true
envelope.summary carries a deterministic clause noting one high-severity warning, alongside the unchanged warnings array entry
